Thermodynamic limit

Words: 26
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
The thermodynamic limit sends particle number and volume to infinity at fixed intensive quantities such as number density. Distinct symmetry-breaking phases become sharply defined in this limit.

Virial expansion

Words: 78 Articles: 2
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
The virial expansion expresses the free energy or pressure of a dilute system as a power series in number density whose coefficients encode few-body interactions.

Second virial coefficient (B2​)

Words: 32
Virial expansion OurBigBook.com
For particles with pair potential U, the second virial coefficient is
B2​=21​∫[1−e−U(r)/(kB​T)]dr,
(1)
with the integration measure adapted to the available relative configurations. Repulsion contributes positively and attraction negatively.

Cluster expansion

Words: 21
Virial expansion OurBigBook.com
The cluster expansion organizes the logarithm of a dilute interacting system's canonical partition function as a sum over connected clusters built from Mayer bonds.

Pair potential (u(r))

Words: 90 Articles: 3
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
A pair potential assigns an interaction energy u(∣xi​−xj​∣) to each pair of particles. A pairwise-additive system has U=∑i<j​u(∣xi​−xj​∣).

Mayer f-function (f(r)=e−u(r)/(kB​T)−1)

Words: 20
Pair potential OurBigBook.com
The Mayer f-function packages the departure of a pair's Boltzmann factor from one and is the basic bond in the dilute-gas cluster expansion.

Hard-sphere gas

Words: 47 Articles: 1
Pair potential OurBigBook.com
A hard-sphere gas has u(r)=+∞ below the contact separation and u(r)=0 above it, so particles cannot overlap.

Excluded volume

Words: 30
Hard-sphere gas OurBigBook.com
The excluded volume is the volume of relative positions forbidden to another particle. For hard spheres of radius r0​, that forbidden region is a sphere of radius 2r0​.

Free-energy density (f)

Words: 21
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
A free-energy density is free energy per unit volume. Its minima with respect to unconstrained order parameters determine homogeneous equilibrium states.

Spin model

Words: 330 Articles: 11
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
A spin model assigns a discrete or continuous spin variable to each site of a lattice or vertex of a graph and gives interacting configurations a Boltzmann factor. Spin models describe collective order and phase transitions in magnetic and other many-body systems.

Ising model

Words: 290 Articles: 10
Spin model OurBigBook.com
The Ising model assigns spins σv​∈{−1,1} to graph vertices with probability proportional to exp(β∑uv​σu​σv​) in zero external field.

Transfer matrix for the one-dimensional Ising model

Words: 33
Ising model OurBigBook.com
For nearest-neighbour interactions, a two-by-two transfer matrix assigns one Boltzmann factor to every adjacent spin pair. With periodic boundary conditions, summing all spin configurations gives the partition function as the trace of a power of this matrix.

Blume–Capel model

Words: 27
Ising model OurBigBook.com
The Blume–Capel model is a spin model with σi​∈{−1,0,1} and Hamiltonian
H=−J∑⟨i,j⟩​σi​σj​+D∑i​σi2​−h∑i​σi​.
(2)
Competition between the Ising interaction and the single-ion anisotropy D produces a tricritical point in its phase diagram.

Glauber dynamics

Words: 33
Ising model OurBigBook.com
Glauber dynamics is a local Markov chain for a spin system. In its heat-bath form, each step chooses one vertex and resamples that spin from its conditional Gibbs distribution given all other spins.

Free boundary condition

Words: 21
Ising model OurBigBook.com
A free boundary condition retains only interactions whose endpoints both lie in the finite volume and imposes no exterior spin values.

Plus boundary condition

Words: 25
Ising model OurBigBook.com
A plus boundary condition fixes every exterior spin adjacent to the finite volume to +1. The increasing-volume limit selects the maximal infinite-volume Gibbs state.

Peierls contour

Words: 32
Ising model OurBigBook.com
A Peierls contour is a dual-lattice boundary separating clusters of opposite Ising spins. Flipping the spins inside a contour of size m changes its Boltzmann weight by the factor e−2βm.

One-dimensional Ising correlation function

Words: 21
Ising model OurBigBook.com
For the zero-field nearest-neighbour Ising model on Z,
⟨σx​σy​⟩=(tanhβ)∣x−y∣.
(3)
More generally, an even ordered product factors over alternating gaps.

Spontaneous magnetization (m(β))

Words: 21
Ising model OurBigBook.com
Spontaneous magnetization is the magnetization that remains after taking the thermodynamic limit and then sending a symmetry-breaking external field to zero.

Random-bond Ising model

Words: 26
Ising model OurBigBook.com
A random-bond Ising model has couplings whose signs or magnitudes vary between edges according to quenched disorder. Negative bonds frustrate neighboring spins that would otherwise align.

Transverse-field Ising model

Words: 33
Ising model OurBigBook.com
The transverse-field Ising model is a quantum spin model with competing Ising exchange and a perpendicular field, for example H=−J∑i​Xi​Xi+1​−h∑i​Zi​. In one dimension its ordered and paramagnetic phases meet at ∣h/J∣=1.

Clock model

Words: 50 Articles: 1
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
The clock model places a planar unit vector at every lattice site but restricts its angle to finitely many equally spaced values. Nearest-neighbour spins usually interact through the cosine of their angular difference.

Four-state clock model

Words: 20
Clock model OurBigBook.com
The four-state clock model permits the four angles 0,π/2,π,3π/2. Its finite discrete symmetry allows finite-temperature long-range order above one spatial dimension.

Classical O(n) lattice model (O(n))

Words: 172 Articles: 5
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
The classical O(n) lattice model assigns a unit vector σx​∈Sn−1 to each lattice site and gives ferromagnetic nearest-neighbour configurations weight proportional to exp(β∑xy​σx​⋅σy​+h∑x​σx​⋅e).

XY model

Words: 25
Classical O(n) lattice model OurBigBook.com
The XY model is the infinite-state limit of the clock model: each spin is a unit vector with a continuous angle and the global symmetry is O(2).

Ginibre inequality

Words: 28
Classical O(n) lattice model OurBigBook.com
For the ferromagnetic O(2) model, cosine observables with nonnegative integer coefficients are positively correlated. One form is
⟨cos(a⋅θ)cos(b⋅θ)⟩≥⟨cos(a⋅θ)⟩⟨cos(b⋅θ)⟩
(4)
for a,b∈Z≥0Λ​, with analogous product forms.

Reflection positivity

Words: 93 Articles: 2
Classical O(n) lattice model OurBigBook.com
A measure is reflection positive for a reflection ϑ when E[FϑF]≥0 for every observable F supported in one reflected half. Product measures and suitable ferromagnetic interactions satisfy this property.

Gaussian domination

Words: 62 Articles: 1
Reflection positivity OurBigBook.com
Gaussian domination bounds the partition function of a reflection-positive spin model under a mean-zero external source by the partition function times a Gaussian exponential involving the inverse lattice Laplacian.
Infrared bound
Words: 33
Gaussian domination OurBigBook.com
The infrared bound controls the nonzero Fourier modes of a spin correlation by the inverse lattice dispersion. Its momentum integral is finite in dimension at least three and can force spontaneous magnetization at low temperature.

Phi-four lattice model (ϕ4)

Words: 56 Articles: 1
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
The phi-four lattice model is a real scalar lattice field with nearest-neighbour gradient energy and an on-site potential gϕ4/4+νϕ2/2.

Random-walk representation of a lattice-field covariance

Words: 36
Phi-four lattice model OurBigBook.com
The Helffer-Sjöstrand random-walk representation expresses a lattice-field covariance as the Green function of a walk in an environment determined by the Hessian of the field potential. A uniformly positive Hessian supplies killing and exponential covariance decay.

Boltzmann equation

Words: 42 Articles: 1
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
The Boltzmann equation evolves a phase-space distribution by balancing free streaming, external forces, and collisions.

Boltzmann hierarchy

Words: 27
Boltzmann equation OurBigBook.com
Expanding an angular distribution in multipoles converts the Boltzmann equation into a hierarchy in which free streaming couples neighboring multipoles and collisions damp or source selected moments.

One-dimensional freely jointed chain

Words: 60 Articles: 2
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
A chain of n links of length a, each pointing independently right or left, has extension
l=(n+​−n−​)a=(2n+​−n)a
(5)
and multiplicity n!/(n+​!n−​!).

Fixed-tension partition function of a one-dimensional chain (Z=(2cosh(τa))n)

Words: 38 Articles: 1
One-dimensional freely jointed chain OurBigBook.com
Weighting each configuration by eτl gives
Z=(eτa+e−τa)n=(2cosh(τa))n,L=∂τ​logZ=natanh(τa).
(6)

Entropic Hooke law for a one-dimensional chain

Words: 22
Fixed-tension partition function of a one-dimensional chain OurBigBook.com
The physical tension is f=kB​Tτ. At small extension,
f∼na2kB​T​L.
(7)
At fixed tension the extension is L=natanh(fa/(kB​T)) and decreases as temperature rises.

State degeneracy

Words: 56 Articles: 3
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
The degeneracy g(l) of a macrostate labelled by l is the number of distinct microstates having that value of l.

Degeneracy factor

Words: 17
State degeneracy OurBigBook.com
A degeneracy factor counts the distinct microscopic states that share the same macroscopic quantum numbers or energy.

Microstate

Words: 10
State degeneracy OurBigBook.com
A microstate is a complete microscopic specification of a system.

Macrostate

Words: 10
State degeneracy OurBigBook.com
A macrostate groups together all microstates that share prescribed macroscopic data.

Quantum ideal-gas statistics

Words: 957 Articles: 37
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
An ideal quantum gas has mean occupation
[exp((E−μ)/(kB​T))∓1]−1,
(8)
with one sign for bosons and the other for fermions.

Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution

Words: 130 Articles: 5
Quantum ideal-gas statistics OurBigBook.com
When E−μ≫kB​T, either quantum occupation law reduces to the classical factor
e−(E−μ)/(kB​T).
(9)

Maxwell-Boltzmann velocity distribution (f(v))
